data.title: AI at Amazon: A case study of brittleness
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
Lorin Hochstein总结了Mihail Eric关于在亚马逊开发AI系统的经历，指出亚马逊的Alexa因缺乏韧性（resilience）而未能保持技术领先。文章通过韧性工程学的视角，分析了亚马逊系统中的三种“脆弱性”模式：

1. **失代偿（Decompensation）**：无法及时获取内部数据和计算资源，导致适应能力枯竭。决策过程过于 hierarchical，拖慢了进展。
   
2. **背道而驰（Working at cross-purposes）**：组织结构过于分散，团队各自为战，内部竞争激烈，缺乏协作，导致整体效率低下。

3. **固守过时行为（Getting stuck in outdated behaviors）**：过于注重客户需求，导致实验性技术研发与产品化目标冲突，创新项目难以推进。

这些因素共同导致亚马逊在AI技术竞赛中落后于竞争对手。文章强调了组织需要在集中与分散之间找到平衡，并灵活适应变化，避免陷入过时的成功模式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亚马逊在机器学习（ML）基础设施建设中的挑战及其组织内部的动态，尤其是与Alexa和AI相关的工作。具体讨论了团队目标的冲突、组织激励机制的不足、技术快速发展的压力以及不同公司（如Google和Amazon）在AI产品化上的成败。

不同观点：
• **yandie**：描述了在亚马逊建立集中式ML基础设施的困难。团队需要不断调整目标，以符合组织的“成功指标”，但最终团队因缺乏资金支持而被解散，因为亚马逊无法为这种基础设施建设提供长期资金。

• **coredog64**：引用了另一篇文章，指出团队没有动力去解决问题，因为解决这些问题不会为团队成员带来晋升机会，导致没有实际行动。

• **taormina**：认为亚马逊的这种情况反映了其内部的“毒性”，即组织文化的问题，而不仅仅是技术或AI相关的问题。

• **PaulHoule**：指出快速发展的基础研究使得在AI领域的投资充满风险，因为技术可能在产品发布时已经过时。此外，提到了一些AI应用的根本性问题，例如环境计算中的挑战，这些问题不会因为更好的模型而得到解决。

• **alex-mohr**：将谷歌在AI产品化上的问题与亚马逊进行了对比，指出了谷歌在组织结构和产品开发上的类似问题，并提到了一些正在进行的改进措施。

• **BryanLegend**：对新版Alexa+给予了积极评价，指出其在语音识别和文本到语音（TTS）方面的显著改进。

• **adolph**：提出了一种不同的观点，认为在资源丰富的组织中，团队之间的竞争和重组可能是好事，因为这能促使团队更高效地完成工作，避免被合并。

补充讨论：
• **激励机制的不足**是多个评论中提到的关键问题，尤其是在coredog64和yandie的评论中，这被视为团队无法持续推进工作的主要原因。

• **技术快速发展的压力**在PaulHoule的评论中被强调，指出即使是大公司如亚马逊和谷歌，也面临技术过时的风险。

• **组织文化和重组的影响**在adolph的评论中被讨论，提出了一种不同的视角，即在资源丰富的组织中，重组可能是激励团队的一种方式。

争议焦点：
• 亚马逊在ML基础设施建设上的失败原因：是由于组织文化的“毒性”还是由于技术发展的固有困难和快速变化的市场环境？

• 团队重组和竞争的利弊：是导致团队解散和资源浪费的原因，还是激励团队高效工作的方式？

这些观点共同描绘了亚马逊和谷歌在AI和ML领域面临的多重挑战，既有组织内部的问题，也有外部技术环境的压力。

44247998.article_content:
Lorin Hochstein
resilience
,
systems
June 8, 2025
4 Minutes
A year ago, Mihail Eric wrote a blog post detailing his experiences working on AI inside Amazon:
How Alexa Dropped the Ball on Being the Top Conversational System on the Planet
. It’s a great first-person account, with lots of detail of the issues that kept Amazon from keeping up with its peers in the LLM space. From my perspective, Eric’s post makes a great case study in what resilience engineering researchers refer to as
brittleness
, which is a term that the researchers use to refer to as a kind of opposite of resilience.
In the paper
Basic Patterns in How Adaptive Systems Fail
, the researchers David Woods and Matthieu Branlat note that brittle systems tend to suffer from the following three patterns:
Decompensation
: exhausting capacity to adapt as challenges cascade
Working at cross-purposes
: behavior that is locally adaptive but globally maladaptive
Getting stuck in outdated behaviors
: the world changes but the system remains stuck in what were previously adaptive strategies (over-relying on past successes)
Eric’s post demonstrates how all three of these patterns were evident within Amazon.
Decompensation
It would take weeks to get access to any internal data for analysis or experiments
…
Experiments had to be run in resource-limited compute environments. Imagine trying to train a transformer model when all you can get a hold of is CPUs. Unacceptable for a company sitting on one of the largest collections of accelerated hardware in the world.
If you’ve ever seen a service fall over after receiving a spike in external requests, you’ve seen a
decompensation
system failure. This happens when a system isn’t able to keep up with the demands that are placed upon on it.
In organizations, you can see the decompensation failure pattern emerge when decision-making is very hierarchical: you end up having to wait for the decision request to make its way up to someone who has the authority to make the decision, and then make its way down again. In the meantime, the world isn’t standing still waiting for that decision to be made.
As described in the
Bad Technical Process
section of Eric’s post, Amazon was not able to keep up with the rate at which its competitors were making progress on developing AI technology, even though Amazon had both the talent and the compute resources necessary in order to make progress. The people inside the organization who needed the resources weren’t able to get them in a timely fashion. That slowed down AI development and, consequently, they got lapped by their competitors.
Working at cross-purposes
Alexa’s org structure was decentralized by design meaning there were multiple small teams working on sometimes identical problems across geographic locales.
This introduced an almost Darwinian flavor to org dynamics where teams scrambled to get their work done to avoid getting reorged and subsumed into a competing team.
The consequence was an organization plagued by antagonistic mid-managers that had little interest in collaborating for the greater good of Alexa and only wanted to preserve their own fiefdoms.
My group by design was intended to span projects, whereby we found teams that aligned with our research/product interests and urged them to collaborate on ambitious efforts. The resistance and lack of action we encountered was soul-crushing.
Where
decompensation
is a consequence of poor centralization,
working at cross-purposes
is a consequence of poor decentralization. In a decentralized organization, the individual units are able to work more quickly, but there’s a risk of
alignment
: enabling everyone to row faster isn’t going to help if they’re rowing in different directions.
In the
Fragmented Org Structures
section of Eric’s writeup, he goes into vivid, almost painful detail about how Amazon’s decentralized org structure worked against them.
Getting stuck in outdated behaviors
Alexa was viciously customer-focused which I believe is admirable and a principle every company should practice. Within Alexa, this meant that every engineering and science effort had to be aligned to some downstream product.
That did introduce tension for our team because we were supposed to be taking experimental bets for the platform’s future. These bets couldn’t be baked into product without hacks or shortcuts in the typical quarter as was the expectation.
So we had to constantly justify our existence to senior leadership and massage our projects with metrics that could be seen as more customer-facing.
…
This introduced product/science conflict in every weekly meeting to track the project’s progress leading to manager churn every few months and an eventual sunsetting of the effort.
I’m generally not a fan of management books, but
What got you here won’t get you there
is a pretty good summary of the third failure pattern: when organizations continue to apply approaches that were well-suited to problems in the past but are ill-suited to problem

Lorin Hochstein总结了Mihail Eric关于在亚马逊开发AI系统的经历，指出亚马逊的Alexa因缺乏韧性（resilience）而未能保持技术领先。文章通过韧性工程学的视角，分析了亚马逊系统中的三种“脆弱性”模式：

1. **失代偿（Decompensation）**：无法及时获取内部数据和计算资源，导致适应能力枯竭。决策过程过于 hierarchical，拖慢了进展。
   
2. **背道而驰（Working at cross-purposes）**：组织结构过于分散，团队各自为战，内部竞争激烈，缺乏协作，导致整体效率低下。

3. **固守过时行为（Getting stuck in outdated behaviors）**：过于注重客户需求，导致实验性技术研发与产品化目标冲突，创新项目难以推进。

这些因素共同导致亚马逊在AI技术竞赛中落后于竞争对手。文章强调了组织需要在集中与分散之间找到平衡，并灵活适应变化，避免陷入过时的成功模式。
44247998.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亚马逊在机器学习（ML）基础设施建设中的挑战及其组织内部的动态，尤其是与Alexa和AI相关的工作。具体讨论了团队目标的冲突、组织激励机制的不足、技术快速发展的压力以及不同公司（如Google和Amazon）在AI产品化上的成败。

不同观点：
• **yandie**：描述了在亚马逊建立集中式ML基础设施的困难。团队需要不断调整目标，以符合组织的“成功指标”，但最终团队因缺乏资金支持而被解散，因为亚马逊无法为这种基础设施建设提供长期资金。

• **coredog64**：引用了另一篇文章，指出团队没有动力去解决问题，因为解决这些问题不会为团队成员带来晋升机会，导致没有实际行动。

• **taormina**：认为亚马逊的这种情况反映了其内部的“毒性”，即组织文化的问题，而不仅仅是技术或AI相关的问题。

• **PaulHoule**：指出快速发展的基础研究使得在AI领域的投资充满风险，因为技术可能在产品发布时已经过时。此外，提到了一些AI应用的根本性问题，例如环境计算中的挑战，这些问题不会因为更好的模型而得到解决。

• **alex-mohr**：将谷歌在AI产品化上的问题与亚马逊进行了对比，指出了谷歌在组织结构和产品开发上的类似问题，并提到了一些正在进行的改进措施。

• **BryanLegend**：对新版Alexa+给予了积极评价，指出其在语音识别和文本到语音（TTS）方面的显著改进。

• **adolph**：提出了一种不同的观点，认为在资源丰富的组织中，团队之间的竞争和重组可能是好事，因为这能促使团队更高效地完成工作，避免被合并。

补充讨论：
• **激励机制的不足**是多个评论中提到的关键问题，尤其是在coredog64和yandie的评论中，这被视为团队无法持续推进工作的主要原因。

• **技术快速发展的压力**在PaulHoule的评论中被强调，指出即使是大公司如亚马逊和谷歌，也面临技术过时的风险。

• **组织文化和重组的影响**在adolph的评论中被讨论，提出了一种不同的视角，即在资源丰富的组织中，重组可能是激励团队的一种方式。

争议焦点：
• 亚马逊在ML基础设施建设上的失败原因：是由于组织文化的“毒性”还是由于技术发展的固有困难和快速变化的市场环境？

• 团队重组和竞争的利弊：是导致团队解散和资源浪费的原因，还是激励团队高效工作的方式？

这些观点共同描绘了亚马逊和谷歌在AI和ML领域面临的多重挑战，既有组织内部的问题，也有外部技术环境的压力。

data.author: baby-yoda
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GLP-1受体激动剂（GLP-1 RAs）与糖尿病患者新生年龄相关性黄斑变性（nAMD）风险之间的潜在关联及其研究方法的有效性。

不同观点：
• [mh-] 强调研究结果显示，暴露于GLP-1 RAs的糖尿病患者中，发生nAMD的患者数量是未暴露患者的两倍多。他认为这一背景很重要，可能会影响对标题的理解。

• [woliveirajr] 指出研究涉及139,000名患者，nAMD的发生率从0.1%增加到0.2%，即139名患者在3年内发展为黄斑变性。他认为需要权衡GLP-1 RAs对糖尿病患者的整体益处（特别是生活质量的改善）与可能增加的黄斑变性风险。

• [jmward01] 对研究的设计提出质疑，指出研究中并未明确说明是否进行了随机分组，这可能导致选择偏差。他怀疑是否因为病情更严重的患者更有可能接受GLP-1 RAs治疗，从而影响了结果。他希望了解研究如何控制这种潜在偏差。

• [declan_roberts] 强调年龄相关性黄斑变性本身是由糖尿病引起的，认为如果不使用GLP-1 RAs控制血糖，黄斑变性的发生率可能会更高。他暗示GLP-1 RAs可能实际上在控制病情进展方面具有积极作用。

• [davikr] 和 [blake929] 仅引用原文中“糖尿病患者”这一关键信息，未发表进一步评论。

补充讨论：
• 研究设计中的选择偏差是一个重要关注点，特别是是否进行了随机分组以确保两组患者具有可比性。
• GLP-1 RAs在控制血糖和改善糖尿病患者生活质量方面的潜在益处是否足以抵消可能增加的nAMD风险，也是一个值得讨论的权衡问题。
• 研究背景中关于糖尿病与年龄相关性黄斑变性之间的固有联系为理解研究结果提供了重要上下文。

主要讨论点：Elon Musk及其公司X在商业行为中的策略和争议，包括与供应商的付款纠纷、法律诉讼以及广告商关系。

不同观点：
• [ohashi] 认为X平台通过不支付账单来对供应商施加压力，并希望亚马逊停止服务直到账单支付，以此来检验谁在这场博弈中拥有真正的 leverage。该评论带有讽刺语气，暗示对Musk做法的不满。

• [cosmicgadget] 将这种情况比作“暴徒统治”，并提到X可能更担心成为像哈佛和Perkins Coïe那样的诉讼目标，暗示法律风险和公众形象问题。

• [jasoncartwright] 仅提供了一个存档链接，没有详细阐述观点，但可能意在引导读者查看相关信息。

• [a_shovel] 质疑X通过起诉未在其平台上投放广告的公司所获得的广告收入，是否足以覆盖诉讼成本，暗示这种策略可能在经济上并不合理。

• [rurp] 批评Musk自称是精英治理的捍卫者，却依赖关系密切的富人朋友帮助推动公司让步，特别提到 activist investor Nelson Peltz 在Unilever谈判中的作用。

• [abeppu] 回顾Musk收购Twitter后声称平台存在大量机器人流量，并质疑广告商对于展示内容和平台政治关联的顾虑，提出广告商是否会怀疑展示给真实人类的印象数量。

• [yablak] 以讽刺的方式评论Musk的付款策略，暗示其行为违背常规商业道德。

• [DoctorOW] 引用了Musk的一条推文，质疑是否存在法律先例强迫他购买迪士尼的新电影，暗示Musk在公共言论中涉及的法律问题。

补充讨论：
评论中对Musk及其公司X的商业策略存在明显争议，尤其是对供应商付款问题和法律诉讼策略的批评。此外，广告商的顾虑和平台流量真实性问题也被提出，显示出X平台在商业运营中的多重挑战。评论者对Musk的领导风格和公共言论也存在不同程度的质疑和讽刺。

data.title: DuckDB Is a Protocol
data.author: summer_avery
data.article_summary: 文章主要观点是，DuckDB表面上是一个快速的OLAP数据库，但实际上它更像是一种“协议”。文章指出，DuckDB不仅在各种应用场景中高度嵌入（如前端、后端、数据管道等），还提供了一种各层通用的语言（SQL语法），促进了不同层之间的通信。DuckDB的跨编程语言兼容性和一致的查询结果使其具备协议的特性。文章预测，DuckDB未来可能会取代S3 Select等技术，并解决分布式数据处理的难题。最终，DuckDB不仅是一种工具，更是开发者构建产品的基石，具备协议的关键属性。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44247545.article_content:
You’ve probably heard that DuckDB is the fastest OLAP database, beating brand names like Clickhouse on
their own benchmarks
. You’ve probably
read
that DuckDB is the worlds most downloaded database, with 30k stars on Github and over 20M monthly downloads via Python alone. You’ve probably bought in to DuckDBs marketing, which states that it is a “fast analytical database system”.
Unfortunately, it’s all a lie. DuckDB isn’t a database at all,
DuckDB is a protocol
masquerading as a database, and understanding this is key to knowing what is going to happen next in data.
With few exceptions, every application developed in the last fifty years has been built atop two things: protocols and databases. Databases are useful constructs to store and retrieve data, but protocols drive innovation.
A protocol can yield a seismic shift for humanity (TCP/IP), alter the way we communicate (SMTP/IMAP/POP3), or even just simplify the way computers talk to each other (JSON). A great database is a wonderful tool, and DuckDB is that, but it’s also already proving itself to be the building block for the next generation of data.
Let’s test our hypothesis and hold DuckDB’s little webbed feet to the “it’s a protocol” fire.
Our “Technology Is A Protocol” rubric:
Embeds into every part of the application stack; front, back, glue in between.
Provides a common language to facilitate communication between layers.
Opens a channel for external communication.
Serves as raw scaffolding on which developers can build products.
Embed everywhere
Need a data wrangling engine for the front end layer? DuckDB WASM. Need a transformations workhorse for ingest pipelines? DuckDB via Python. Need a blazing fast query engine for an enterprise lakehouse? DuckDB in a container. Need a one off or scheduled process that generates parquet and squirrels it away in object storage for later? DuckDB in a Lambda. No question on this one, we pass the embed test.
Common language for all layers
All databases have their own SQL syntax and DuckDB is no different. DuckDB’s is ergonomic and dripping with syntactic sugar, but a SQL syntax does not a protocol make. Yet, there is something special here, a compounding effect. DuckDB’s embed-ability, combined with it’s SQL syntax, creates a universal language that all layers of the stack speak. Having a single data language, without transmogrification, within each component of your application stack is as much of an unlock as is, say, using GRPC/ProtocolBuffers (a protocol!) to pass raw data around.
A tiny tangent
Speaking of ProtoBuffs, maybe the best way to show that DuckDB is a protocol is to take something that is definitively a protocol and draw parallels. ProtoBuffs give us benefits like cross-programming-language compatibility, generated clients, and strong typing. With DuckDB we get similar, but not identical, effects. Cross-programming-language compatibility is replaced by the fact that DuckDB SQL is DuckDB SQL regardless of if you are calling it from C, Python, or Node. “Generated clients” are served by DuckDB releases that speak said syntax, available for virtually any programming language and operating system you might be building on. Finally, strong typing guarantees are made by virtue of the fact that DuckDB SQL run in different environments, but against the same dataset, will result in consistent output (excepting of course the situations
listed here
).
Back to the rubric, connecting with others
Embeda-bility and common language are the obvious givens, but to see the true power of DuckDB as a protocol we need to make guesses as to what is
going
to happen in the near future. How long will it be until AWS replaces
S3 Select
🪦 with S3 Query powered by DuckDB reading S3 Tables? Inevitable. How long will it be until someone cracks the “distributed duckdb” puzzle (getting closer
Smallpond
!) and knocks down the final “range anxiety” data volume mental trap locking people into their legacy data warehouses? It’s coming.
There are infinite more future DuckDB scenarios, but they all arrive at the same point. These unlocks, tools, and next generations system are being built on the same query execution engine and speaking the same SQL syntax. It doesn’t matter what the rails of communication are between them. HTTP, GRPC, ODBC, or Arrow Flight, they will all work seamlessly together because DuckDB is itself the protocol and the communication rails are just an implementation detail.
But can you build on it?
The final point, and the one that matters most; does this technology serve as scaffolding for developers to build products? I don’t think we’ve ever seen a tool, specifically in the data space, which has been adopted
into products
as quickly as we’re seeing with DuckDB. Speaking from our own experience, by using DuckDB in every part of our product we’ve been able to build BI, warehousing, and ETL at what seems like an unbelievable pace.
Confirmed, it’s a protocol
All checks passed, DuckDB is a protocol. We believe embracin

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容的版权争议及对创意领域的影响

不同观点：
• [beardyw] 认为AI生成内容虽然在效率上更高，但并没有带来真正的创新。现有的规则没有考虑到“灵感来源于他者”这一部分，对创意工作者的保护不足。

• [waffletower] 主张公平使用原则，认为社会不应该变成“每想法都得付费”的状态，隐含对过度保护知识产权的担忧。

• [Chihuahua0633] 并未直接讨论文章内容，而是提供了一个绕过付费墙的链接，方便其他人阅读文章，保持讨论的开放性。

• [codazoda] 分享了个人经历，指出AI生成的图像与其已知IP（如Pixar的《Cars》）非常相似，质疑这种生成是否涉及版权侵犯，虽然承认某些元素可能不可版权化。

• [deafpolygon] 提出应该起诉那些使用AI工具生成侵权内容的人，而不是工具本身，暗示责任在于使用者而非技术。

• [ChrisArchitect] 对事件的背景有所了解，认为迪士尼和环球影城的法律行动是逐步升级的，暗示这些公司可能早已采取行动，只是现在才被广泛报道。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的版权问题，特别是当这些内容与已有IP非常相似时，是否构成侵权。
• 不同的讨论者对版权保护的范围和执行方式有不同看法，有的侧重创意保护，有的则关注公共领域的自由使用。
• 链接分享和事件背景补充进一步丰富了讨论的维度，展示了实际操作中可能遇到的法律和伦理问题。

不同观点：
• [beardyw] 认为AI生成内容虽然在效率上更高，但并没有带来真正的创新。现有的规则没有考虑到“灵感来源于他者”这一部分，对创意工作者的保护不足。

• [waffletower] 主张公平使用原则，认为社会不应该变成“每想法都得付费”的状态，隐含对过度保护知识产权的担忧。

• [Chihuahua0633] 并未直接讨论文章内容，而是提供了一个绕过付费墙的链接，方便其他人阅读文章，保持讨论的开放性。

• [codazoda] 分享了个人经历，指出AI生成的图像与其已知IP（如Pixar的《Cars》）非常相似，质疑这种生成是否涉及版权侵犯，虽然承认某些元素可能不可版权化。

• [deafpolygon] 提出应该起诉那些使用AI工具生成侵权内容的人，而不是工具本身，暗示责任在于使用者而非技术。

• [ChrisArchitect] 对事件的背景有所了解，认为迪士尼和环球影城的法律行动是逐步升级的，暗示这些公司可能早已采取行动，只是现在才被广泛报道。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的版权问题，特别是当这些内容与已有IP非常相似时，是否构成侵权。
• 不同的讨论者对版权保护的范围和执行方式有不同看法，有的侧重创意保护，有的则关注公共领域的自由使用。
• 链接分享和事件背景补充进一步丰富了讨论的维度，展示了实际操作中可能遇到的法律和伦理问题。

The Federal Communications Commission is facing widespread criticism after threatening to revoke EchoStar licenses for spectrum bands that rival firms, including SpaceX, want to take over. Opposition to license revocations came from conservatives, telecom consumer advocates, and some industry groups.
The Free State Foundation, a free-market group that has generally supported Republican priorities at the FCC, filed
comments
saying that "arbitrary" decisions would create instability in the market for wireless broadband deployment. EchoStar is now facing regulatory uncertainty less than a year after obtaining deadline extensions for its wireless network buildout, the Free State Foundation said:
There is widespread agreement that constructing and operating wireless broadband networks depends on significant private market investment. Legal stability is a necessary ingredient for the operation of any marketplace conducive to competition and growth, including today's dynamic wireless market. Before risking their money in commercial ventures, private investors reasonably seek assurance that their interests and rights will be protected from changes in the rules or agency actions that are arbitrary or unforeseen... Rescission of deadline extension orders granted months earlier undoubtedly creates a type of regulatory uncertainty.
As
previously reported
, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr directed agency staff to investigate EchoStar's compliance with obligations to provide nationwide 5G service under the terms of its spectrum licenses. EchoStar bought Dish Network in December 2023 and offers wireless service under the Boost Mobile brand.
Carr, who became FCC Chairman in January 2025 after President Trump's second term began, disagreed with last year's decision to give EchoStar an extension from June 2025 to June 2028. His threat to EchoStar made it clear he is considering a reversal of that decision.
EchoStar has been skipping debt-interest payments because of the probe. The Wall Street Journal
reported
Friday that "EchoStar is considering a chapter 11 bankruptcy filing as the company vies to shield its cache of wireless spectrum licenses from the threat of revocation by federal regulators."
FCC action could help Starlink
A Carr
letter to EchoStar
last month said the company "negotiated behind closed doors during the previous Administration" to extend its deadline and avoid "the agreed-upon consequences" for failing to meet its buildout obligations. Those potential consequences include "the loss of its spectrum licenses and significant financial payments," the Carr letter said.
EchoStar losing licenses could help Starlink operator SpaceX, which alleges that EchoStar hasn't properly utilized its spectrum and urged the FCC to reallocate frequencies in the 2 GHz band "for sharing among next-generation satellite systems." Separately, Vermont-based VTel Wireless asked the FCC to reconsider its 2024 decision to extend EchoStar construction deadlines for spectrum in several bands. That includes the 2 GHz band SpaceX complained about and spectrum in 600 MHz and 700 MHz bands.
When Carr sent his letter, the FCC opened one proceeding seeking public comment on EchoStar's use of its 2 GHz spectrum and another on the VTel Wireless petition. There was a June 6 deadline for comments on both.
Michael O'Rielly, a Republican who served as an FCC commissioner from 2013 to 2020, released a
statement
supporting EchoStar. "Companies should receive fair treatment by the government and be able to rely on agreements entered into with government agencies," O'Rielly said. His statement praised EchoStar's attempt "to complete a modern Open RAN 5G network with American vendors" and said that "the market should determine whether its wireless offering can be successful."
Consumer advocates at Public Knowledge and New America's Open Technology Institute
told the FCC
that "any proceeding that jeopardizes EchoStar's existence will harm competition, hurt American consumers, and jeopardize national security."
Network contractors say jobs are at stake
About 30 general contractors that are working with EchoStar to deploy its 5G network
urged the FCC
to leave its earlier decision in place. "Together, we have helped [EchoStar] deploy more than 24,000 cell sites and counting, covering more than 80 percent of the US population (268 million Americans)... EchoStar's deployment has created many jobs in local communities across the countries—both at our companies and those in the broader wireless infrastructure ecosystem," the filing said. "Any actions undertaken by the Commission that would result in halting EchoStar's wireless buildout would have a direct negative impact on these jobs and would also pose significant economic challenges for our businesses."

data.title: "Localhost tracking" explained. It could cost Meta €32B
data.author: donohoe
data.article_summary: Meta被发现使用“本地主机追踪”技术绕过Android的隐私保护，能够在用户使用VPN、浏览器的无痕模式以及拒绝或删除 cookies的情况下，继续追踪其网络活动并识别其真实身份。这种方法通过Facebook/Instagram应用后台运行，并利用Meta的追踪脚本在移动浏览器内传递用户数据。该行为违反了GDPR、DSA和DMA等多项法规，可能导致累计高达320亿欧元的罚款。这一技术引发了隐私保护方面的重大争议，并可能面临创纪录的罚款。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta（Facebook 和 Instagram）通过Android应用进行隐蔽的网络跟踪行为，包括通过localhost进行数据传输以及利用WebRTC技术绕过用户隐私保护措施。讨论还涉及隐私侵犯的法律责任、技术漏洞以及用户对大公司应用的不信任等问题。

不同观点：
• **对Meta历史行为的批评**：多位用户提到Meta（包括其前身Facebook）有不良历史记录，例如2014年Android Twitter应用收集用户安装应用列表，以及通过HTTPS流量监控应用流行度等行为。用户认为Meta的跟踪行为是持续且具有欺骗性的，目的是支持其广告业务。
  
• **工程师和产品经理的个人责任**：有评论提出，实施这些跟踪技术的工程师和产品经理应承担个人责任，因为他们的行为是故意且有记录的，应该为这些行为承担法律后果。

• **技术漏洞和解决方案**：一些用户指出Android系统允许应用在未经许可的情况下打开端口和相互通信，而浏览器也允许随机域访问localhost服务。有建议提出，应该通过默认禁用WebRTC或增加权限提示来防止这些行为。

• **用户责任和信任问题**：有观点认为，用户不应该信任来自大型广告公司（如Meta）的应用，特别是在隐私保护方面。同时，也有评论指出，用户在点击同意权限时往往不够谨慎，导致隐私泄露。

• **Meta的动机和市场竞争**：有评论认为Meta的跟踪行为是为了测试和验证其其他跟踪技术的有效性，并保持其在广告市场的主导地位。部分用户认为Meta正试图在下一代平台（如AR或VR）到来之前保持其市场优势。

• **法律和道德问题**：有讨论提到Meta的行为可能不仅仅是民事责任，而是涉及未经授权的数据窃取和违反GDPR的刑事犯罪。用户对Meta通过技术手段绕过用户隐私保护感到愤怒，并质疑其行为是否构成犯罪。

补充讨论：
• **平台和媒体反应**：有用户质疑为什么这一新闻没有在Hacker News首页停留很长时间，认为其具备成为热门话题的所有要素，包括用户欺骗、隐私保护绕过、大公司行为等。

• **其他公司的类似行为**：有评论提到Yandex多年来的类似行为未被注意到，质疑为什么Facebook去年才开始启用这种技术，是否存在行业普遍性问题。

争议焦点：
• Meta通过隐蔽手段进行用户数据跟踪的道德和法律责任问题，以及Android系统和浏览器在保护用户隐私方面的技术漏洞，是讨论的核心争议点。用户对Meta的行为感到愤怒，并对其动机和市场策略提出质疑。

What happened?
Meta devised an ingenious system (“localhost tracking”) that bypassed Android’s sandbox protections to identify you while browsing on your mobile phone — even if you used a VPN, the browser’s incognito mode, and refused or deleted cookies in every session.
Next, we preview what may (and should) become the combined sanctioning smackdown of the century, and then we explain — in simple terms (because it’s complicated) — what Meta was doing.
It smells like record fine spirit
Meta faces simultaneous liability under the following regulations, listed from least to most severe: GDPR, DSA, and DMA (I’m not even including the ePrivacy Directive because it’s laughable).
GDPR, DMA, and DSA protect different legal interests, so the penalties under each can be imposed cumulatively.
The combined theoretical maximum risk amounts to approximately €32 billion** (4% + 6% + 10% of Meta’s global annual revenue, which surpassed €164 billion in 2024).
Maximum fines have never before been applied simultaneously, but some might say these scoundrels have earned it.
If you want to go straight to the breakdown of infractions and penalties, click
here
.
You’re reading ZERO PARTY DATA. The newsletter about the crazy crazy world news from a data protection perspective by Jorge García Herrero and Darío López Rincón.
In the spare time this newsletter leaves us, we like to solve complicated issues about GDPR & AI Act. If you’ve got one of those, give us a little wave. Or contact us by email at jgh(at)jorgegarciaherrero.com.
Subscribe
What is “localhost tracking”?
Below is a simplified explanation of a very technical process,
rigorously detailed on the website set up by the researchers who uncovered Meta’s latest major blow
to the GDPR specifically, and to other regulations more broadly, as we’ll see.
Credit where it’s due — it’s ingenious. Ingenious in the sense of breaking (yet again) the record for a privacy-related fine, but hey!... ingenious.
This is the process through which Meta (Facebook/Instagram) managed to link what you do in your browser (for example, visiting a news site or an online store) with your real identity (your Facebook or Instagram account), even if you never logged into your account through the browser or anything like that.
Meta accomplishes this through two invisible channels that exchange information:
(i) The Facebook or Instagram app running in the background on your phone, even when you’re not using it.
(ii) Meta’s tracking scripts (the now-pulled illegal brainchild uncovered last week), which operate inside your mobile web browser.
Thanks
to the outstanding human beings who revealed this scandal:
Tim Vlummens, Narseo Vallina-Rodriguez, Nipuna Weerasekara, Gunes Acar, and Aniketh Girish
.
The entire flow of the _fbp cookie from web to native and the server is as follows:
The user opens the native Facebook or Instagram app, which eventually is sent to the background and creates a background service to listen for incoming traffic on a TCP port (12387 or 12388) and a UDP port (the first unoccupied port in 12580-12585). Users must be logged-in with their credentials on the apps.
The user opens their browser and visits a website integrating the Meta Pixel.
At this stage, websites may ask for consent depending on the website's and visitor's locations.
The Meta Pixel script sends the
_fbp cookie
to the native Instagram or Facebook app via WebRTC (STUN) SDP Munging.
The Meta Pixel script also sends the _fbp value in a request to https://www.facebook.com/tr along with other parameters such as page URL (dl), website and browser metadata, and the
event type
(ev) (e.g., PageView, AddToCart, Donate, Purchase).
The Facebook or Instagram apps receive the _fbp cookie from the Meta Pixel JavaScript running on the browser. The apps transmit _fbp as a GraphQL mutation to (https://graph[.]facebook[.]com/graphql) along with other persistent user identifiers, linking users' fbp ID (web visit) with their Facebook or Instagram account.
I'll explain it step by step, like you're five years old
If I understood it, you can too — trust me.

data.title: Java 25's new CPU-Time Profiler
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在OpenJDK 25中引入的实验性CPU时间性能分析工具（CPU-time profiler），该工具旨在帮助开发者发现代码中的性能问题，相比当前的采样器具有明显优势。当前的JFR（Java Flight Recorder）分析策略每隔一定时间（如10或20毫秒）对线程进行采样，但由于对Java线程的优先采样以及系统并行线程数量的影响，可能导致采样不准确，且无法区分CPU时间和执行时间。新工具通过CPU时间采样，可以更好地分析计算密集型方法对CPU资源的消耗，从而优化程序吞吐量。下周的博客将深入探讨其技术细节。

44246557.article_content:
More than three years in the making, with a concerted effort starting last year, my CPU-time profiler
landed
in Java with OpenJDK 25. It’s an experimental new profiler/method sampler that helps you find performance issues in your code, having distinct advantages over the current sampler. This is what this week’s and next week’s blog posts are all about. This week, I will cover why we need a new profiler and what information it provides; next week, I’ll cover the technical internals that go beyond what’s written in the JEP. I will quote the
JEP 509
quite a lot, thanks to Ron Pressler; it reads like a well-written blog post in and of itself.
Before I show you its details, I want to focus on what the current default method profiler in JFR does:
Current JFR Profiling Strategy
JDK 25’s default method profiler also changed, as my previous blog post,
Taming the Bias: Unbiased* Safepoint-Based Stack Walking in JFR
, described. However, the profiling strategy remained the same.
At every interval, say 10 or 20 milliseconds, five threads running in Java and one in native Java are picked from the list of threads and sampled. This thread list is iterated linearly, and threads not in the requested state are skipped (
source
).
Problems?
This strategy has problems, as also covered in
a talk by Jaroslav Bachorik and me at this year’s FOSDEM
:
https://video.fosdem.org/2025/ua2118/fosdem-2025-4848-advancing-java-profiling-achieving-precision-and-stability-with-jfr-ebpf-and-user-context.mp4
The aggressive subsampling means that the effective sampling interval depends on the number of cores and the parallelism of your system. Say we have a large machine on which 32 threads can run in parallel. Then JFR on samples at most 19%, turning a sampling rate of 10ms into 53ms. This is an inherent property of wall-clock sampling, as the sampler considers threads on the system. This number can be arbitrarily large, so sub-sampling is necessary.
However, the sampling policy is not true wall-clock sampling, as it prioritizes threads running in Java. Consider a setting where 10 threads run in native and 5 in Java. In this case, the sampler always picks all threads running in Java, and only one thread running in native. This might be confusing and may lead users to the wrong conclusions.
Even if we gloss over this and call the current strategy “execution-time”, it might not be suitable for profiling every application. To quote from the/my JEP (thanks to Ron Pressler for writing most of the JEP text in its final form):
Execution time does not necessarily reflect CPU time. A method that sorts an array, e.g., spends all of its time on the CPU. Its execution time corresponds to the number of CPU cycles it consumes. In contrast, a method that reads from a network socket might spend most of its time idly waiting for bytes to arrive over the wire. Of the time it consumes, only a small portion is spent on the CPU. An execution-time profile will not distinguish between these cases.
Even a program that does a lot of I/O can be constrained by the CPU. A computation-heavy method might consume little execution time compared the program’s I/O operations, thus having little effect on latency — but it might consume most of the program’s CPU cycles, thus affecting throughput. Identifying and optimizing such methods will reduce CPU consumption and improve the program’s throughput — but in order to do so, we need to profile CPU time rather than execution time.
JEP 509: JFR CPU-Time Profiling (Experimental)
Execution-time Example
For example, consider a program,
HttpRequests
, with two threads, each performing HTTP requests. One thread runs a
tenFastRequests
method that makes ten requests, sequentially, to an HTTP endpoint that responds in 10ms; the other runs a
oneSlowRequest
method that makes a single request to an endpoint that responds in 100ms. The average latency of both methods should be about the same, and so the total time spent executing them should be about the same.
We can record a stream of execution-time profiling events like so:
$ java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=profile.jfr,settings=profile.jfc HttpRequests client
JEP 509: JFR CPU-Time Profiling (Experimental)
You can find the program on
GitHub
. Be aware that it requires the server instance to run alongside, start it via
java HttpRequests server

events into the file
profile.jfr
. Each event captures the stack trace of a thread running Java code, thus recording all of the methods currently running on that thread. (The file
profile.jfc
is a JFR configuration file, included in the JDK, that configures the JFR events needed for an execution-time profile.)

jfr
tool included in the JDK:
$ jfr view native-methods profile.jfr

44246557.article_summary: 本文介绍了在OpenJDK 25中引入的实验性CPU时间性能分析工具（CPU-time profiler），该工具旨在帮助开发者发现代码中的性能问题，相比当前的采样器具有明显优势。当前的JFR（Java Flight Recorder）分析策略每隔一定时间（如10或20毫秒）对线程进行采样，但由于对Java线程的优先采样以及系统并行线程数量的影响，可能导致采样不准确，且无法区分CPU时间和执行时间。新工具通过CPU时间采样，可以更好地分析计算密集型方法对CPU资源的消耗，从而优化程序吞吐量。下周的博客将深入探讨其技术细节。

data.title: Scientific Papers: Innovation or Imitation?
data.author: tapanjk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了某些具有开创性思想的学术论文，尽管它们蕴含着推动全新研究方向的潜力，但往往未能引发深入探索，仅产生了一些模仿性工作。例如，1943年的McCulloch-Pitts论文展示了神经网络如何表示某一类逻辑或布尔表达式，但其核心思想未被充分理解，导致连接主义和符号AI之间的对立持续至今。又如George Miller的“7±2”论文揭示了人类在推理时能同时处理的信息量有限，尽管其方法论具有突破性，但后续研究多局限于扩展具体发现。文章指出，学术出版的激励结构导致许多论文更倾向于模仿而非创新，研究者常囿于自身领域的狭隘视角，忽略了跨领域联结和潜在的新研究方向。尽管当前AI研究展现出创新与模仿并存的局面，但仍需警惕研究中的误区和方法论问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术界的创新压力与出版文化

不同观点：
• [empiko] 认为当今科学界的出版压力抑制了创新。为了满足每年发表若干论文的要求，研究人员只能选择简单、迭代性的研究，而没有时间进行创新或验证方法的正确性。举例来说，尽管AI研究火热，但创新率并没有显著提高。

• [kj4211cash] 指出，学术生活主要围绕获取研究经费展开，特别是在STEM领域。为了获得资助，研究人员需要遵循官僚机构设定的具体研究课题，而这些课题往往缺乏创新性。只有最著名的研究人员才有时间和意愿去探索创新。

• [kevinventullo] 认为，虽然许多后续论文仅以很小的方式扩展了原始发现，但它们也间接复制了原始结果，这在应对学术复现危机中具有重要贡献。

• [agarttha] 表示，过多的模仿延缓了创新。系统不奖励高风险研究，创造力未得到应有的重视。负面结果和失败的实验虽然阻碍了职业发展，但却是尝试创新的标志。

• [Daub] 描述了在东南亚大学工作时观察到的学术出版问题，包括重复发表、追逐潮流和可疑的署名等现象。虽然有些学者尝试风险较高的课题，但他们都冒着职业风险。

• [mpascale00] 认为一些观点没有详细阐述，例如在语言学领域，虽然乔姆斯基的工作是基础性的，但目前对工作记忆和行为组合性的理解已经有所进步。

• [birn559] 认为当前的学术出版过程虽不完美，但在中长期内运作良好，且优于任何已知的替代方案。唯一的改进建议是降低期刊成本，由机构支付发表费用，但这不会改变过程的基础。

• [richarlidad] 提出，模仿 precedes 创造，暗示创新可能需要通过模仿奠定基础。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于当前学术出版体系是否真正促进了创新，以及是否有更好的替代方案。
- 讨论中提到的具体问题包括出版压力、资助课题的选择、学术复现危机以及学术界对创新和失败的接受度。
- 有观点指出，创新需要冒险，但现行体制往往不奖励甚至惩罚失败，从而抑制了创新。
- 不同学科的学者对创新的理解和实践存在差异，例如计算机工程与物理学研究的对比。

总结来看，评论主要围绕学术出版压力对创新的影响展开，涉及出版文化的缺陷、资助机制的问题以及可能的改进方向。

44232371.article_content:
Sometimes a paper comes out that has the seeds of a great idea that could lead to a whole new line of pioneering research. But, instead, nothing much happens, except imitative works that do not push the core idea forward at all.
For example the
McCulloch Pitts paper
from 1943 showed how neural networks could represent arbitrary logical or Boolean expressions of a certain class. The paper was well-received at the time, brilliantly executed by co-authors with diverse expertise in neuroscience, logic and computing. Had its signficance been fully grasped, this paper might have, at least notionally, formed a unifying conceptual bridge between the two nascent schools of connectionism and symbolic AI (one can at least hope). But instead, the heated conflict in viewpoints in the field has persisted, even to this day.
Another example is
George Miller’s 7 +/- 2 paper
. This famous result showed humans are able to hold only a small number of pieces of information in mind at the same time while reasoning.  This paper was important not just for the specific result, but for the breakthrough in methodology using rigorous experimental noninvasive methods to discover how human thinking works—a topic we know so little about, even today. However, the followup papers by others, for the most part, only extended or expanded on the specific finding in very minor ways. [1] Thankfully, Miller’s approach did eventually gain influence in more subtle ways.
Of course it’s natural from the incentive structures of publishing that many papers would be primarily derivative rather than original. It’s not a bad thing that, when a pioneering paper comes out, others very quickly write rejoinder papers containing evaluations or minor tweaks of the original result. Not bad, but sometimes we miss the larger implications of the original result and get lost in the details.
Another challenge is stovepiping—we get stuck in our narrow swim lanes for our specific fields and camps of research. [2] We don’t see the broader implications, such as connections and commonalities across fields that could lead to fruitful new directions.
Thankfully, at least to some extent current research in AI shows some mix of both innovation and imitation. Inspired in part by the accelerationist mindset, many new papers appear every day, some with significant new findings and others that are more modest riffs on previous papers.
Notes
[1] Following this line of research on human thought processes could be worthwhile for various reasons. For example, some papers in linguistics state that Chomsky‘s vision for a universal grammar is misguided because the common patterns in human language are entirely explainable by the processing limitations of the human mind. But this claim is made with no justification or methodological rigor of any kind. If I claimed a CPU performs vector addition or atomic operations efficiently because of “the capabilities of the processor,” I would need to provide some supporting evidence, for example, documenting that the CPU has vector processing units or specialized hardware for atomics. The assertions about language structure being shaped by the human mental processing faculty is just an empty truism, unless supported by some amount of scientific rigor and free of the common fallacies of statistical reasoning.
[2] I recently read a paper in linguistics with apparent promise, but the paper totally misconstrued the relationship between Shannon entropy and Kolmogorov complexity. Sadly this paper passed review in a linguistic journal, but if it had had a mathematically inclined reviewer, the problem would have been caught and fixed.

data.title: Sly Stone has died
data.author: brudgers
data.article_summary: Sly Stone，传奇放克乐队Sly and the Family Stone的领袖，于82岁去世。该乐队以融合放克、迷幻音乐及多种音乐风格著称，并在1993年进入摇滚名人堂。乐队成立于1966年，是首个种族融合的美国主要摇滚乐队，凭借单曲《Dance to the Music》和专辑《Stand!》迅速走红，代表作包括《Everyday People》和《Hot Fun in the Summertime》。Sly Stone被视为现代音乐的奠基者之一，但乐队在巅峰期后因药物问题和内部矛盾逐渐衰落。Sly Stone晚年饱受慢性阻塞性肺病困扰，安静离世，但他的音乐遗产将继续影响后代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sly Stone及其音乐的影响和评价

不同观点：
• **Sly Stone的音乐影响深远**：[harry8]提到Sly Stone的演出影响了Stevie Wonder创作《Superstition》等经典作品，类似于历史上天才之间的相互启发（如Haydn和Mozart）。[mykowebhn]通过Sly和Muhammad Ali在电视节目中的互动，强调了Sly在音乐之外作为和平使者的角色。

• **个人情感与回忆**：[plemer]表达了Sly的音乐对他们家庭的美好回忆，音乐代表了夏天的快乐与勇气。[WalterBright]则提到自己从《Dance to the Music》开始成为Sly的粉丝，强调了其音乐的持久影响。

• **对Sly音乐作品的评价**：[funksta]反驳了一种认为Sly在1969年后没有再达到高峰的观点，认为《There's a Riot Goin On》和《Fresh》都是经典且极具影响力的专辑。[pivic]补充说明Sly不仅是出色的表演者和音乐家，还是杰出的词曲作者和制作人，对音乐有着深刻的理解。

• **对Sly生平的反思**：[Bluestein]认为Sly是一个超越时代的天才，他不得不“简化”自己的天才以迎合观众，但在这个过程中定义了一个时代。[MrJagil]分享了一个电视片段，显示Sly在电视上显得神志不清，反映了他的生平复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **推荐作品**：[asveikau]建议听《everyday people》并关注歌词。[coastalpuma]则建议听《There's a riot goin on》以缅怀Sly。[kylebebak]分享了《Everybody Is a Star》的链接。

• **误解与文化背景**：[bosky101]提到自己最初误以为讨论的是Sylvester Stallone，显示了对Sly Stone的陌生。[acomjean]分享了一部关于Sly及其乐队的纪录片，强调了其在旧金山60年代“嬉皮放克”文化中的地位。

争议焦点：Sly Stone是否在1969年后未能再创高峰。这引发了对Sly作品质量和影响力的重新评价。

44229841.article_content:
Sly Stone, pioneering leader of funk band Sly and the Family Stone, dies at 82
Sly and the Family Stone entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1993.
By
Mark Osborne
June 9, 2025, 6:04 PM
2:48
Sly Stone of Sly And The Family Stone poses in London, July 16, 1973.
Michael Putland/Getty Images
Sly Stone, the pioneering leader of the funk band bearing his name, Sly and the Family Stone, has died, according to his family. Stone was 82 years old.
"After a prolonged battle with COPD and other underlying health issues, Sly passed away peacefully, surrounded by his three children, his closest friend, and his extended family," his family said in a statement. "While we mourn his absence, we take solace in knowing that his extraordinary musical legacy will continue to resonate and inspire for generations to come."
Sly Stone of Sly And The Family Stone poses in London, July 16, 1973.
Michael Putland/Getty Images
Stone, whose real name was Sylvester Stewart, formed a band with his brother Freddie and sisters Loretta and Rose at an early age. The band played gospel music, seemingly a far cry from the funk and psychedelia he would later become known for, but Sly and the Family Stone would become known for its blending of music styles.
Sly Stone would answer simply when writing in his 2023 memoir, "Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin)," about how he wanted to be remembered: "Music, just music."
"I don't want to get in people's way and I don't want them to get in my way. I just want to play my songs," he said. "I would do it for nothing."
He was born in Texas in 1943, the second oldest of five children, but his family moved to the San Francisco Bay Area when he was young. He got a job as a disc jockey in the early '60s and played everything from British rock to soul music.
Sly and the Family Stone formed in 1966 as a combination of Sly and his brother Freddie's individual bands. Sister Rose also joined the group. Loretta chose not to pursue music while younger sister Vaetta performed in her own band, Little Sister, and would join Sly and the Family Stone for occasional gigs.
MORE: In Memoriam: Notable people who died in 2025
While Sly was predominantly a guitarist when the band formed, he allowed Freddie to take that role in the new group and mostly played keyboard. However, he was, by many accounts, a musical prodigy. He learned to play guitar, keyboard, bass and the drums as a child.
The Family Stone was the first major American rock band to be racially integrated.
Sly and the Family Stone released its first album in October 1967, "A Whole New Thing," but it received only limited attention. Just a month later, the band would be launched into the stratosphere when it released the single "Dance to the Music."
"Dance to the Music" peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard Pop Singles chart.
"I knew the music worked, but I didn’t know if people would get it," Stone
told The Guardian
in 2023 in a rare interview during the later years of his life. “That’s what happened after the first album -- I poured everything into those songs. Music people liked it, but not everyone was a music person. 'Dance to the Music' came out as a simpler version, and more people understood that."
Sly Stone from the group Sly and the Family Stone performs at the 48th Annual Grammy Awards on Feb. 8, 2006, in Los Angeles.
Mark J. Terrill/AP, FILE
The band -- and Sly in particular -- also quickly came to be known for its high-energy, uptempo live performances. By 1969, after the release of "Stand!" the same year, the band was one of the biggest in the world and Sly was a household name.
"Stand!" featured the song "Everyday People," the group's first No. 1 single, and "Hot Fun in the Summertime," which reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.
"Timing is everything, you can't plan lightning in a bottle, and Sly just happened to come at a time period in which the paradigm shift was gonna change culturally for music," Roots drummer Questlove, who directed the film "Sly Lives!," released in February,
told "Good Morning America."
"He's one of the first Black artists -- really one of the first artists to sort of write confessional, along with [Bob] Dylan -- the idea of not just doing love songs but talking about how you feel inside or political things. ... Everything that was modern music, Sly pretty much built the blueprint.
At the height of the band's fame, the members took the stage at the original Woodstock in August 1969. The band went on stage at 3:30 a.m. on Sunday morning, just after Janis Joplin and just before The Who. The group ripped through an electric medley of hits including "Everyday People," "Dance To The Music," "Music Lover" and "I Want To Take You Higher."
However, it was not long after that the band devolved into drugs, finger-pointing and missed shows. Sly himself admitted in his memoir that he became dependent on cocaine and PCP. The band released several unheralded albums in the '70s but never reached the height of 1969 again. It was the

data.title: LLMs are cheap
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了生成型AI的运营成本其实相对较低，反驳了人们普遍认为像ChatGPT这样的大语言模型（LLM）运行成本高昂的误解。作者通过对比搜索引擎（如Google和Bing）的API价格与LLM的每千次查询成本，发现LLM的成本不仅不高于搜索引擎，甚至低得多，最便宜的LLM模型成本仅为搜索API的十分之一。文章还提到，随着技术进步，LLM的推理成本在两年内下降了1000倍，而这种快速降价让人难以直观理解。因此，关于AI公司因高成本而注定失败的论断并不准确，且对消费者AI业务的盈利模式需要更全面的看法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和搜索API的成本与盈利能力比较

• [tiagod] 提到共享出行和外卖行业曾有过类似的低价阶段，认为AI行业目前也处于这一阶段，且不会永久持续。

• [bustadjustme] 对LLM单个标记输出与搜索结果的比较提出疑问，但随后承认误解了作者的单位换算。

44223448.article_content:
This post is making a point - generative AI is relatively cheap -
that might seem so obvious it doesn't need making. I'm mostly writing it because I've
repeatedly had the same discussion in the past six months where people claim the opposite.
Not only is the misconception still around, but it's not even getting less frequent. This
is mainly written to have a document I can point people at, the next time it repeats.
It seems to be a common, if not a majority, belief that Large
Language Models (in the colloquial sense of "things that are like
ChatGPT") are very expensive to operate. This then leads to a ton
of innumerate analyses about how AI companies must be obviously
doomed, as well as a myopic view on how consumer AI businesses can/will
be monetized.
It's an understandable mistake, since inference was indeed very
expensive at the start of the AI boom, and those costs were talked about
a lot. But inference has gotten cheaper even faster
than models have gotten better, and nobody has an intuition for
something becoming 1000x cheaper in two years. It just doesn't happen.
It doesn't help that the common pricing model ("$ per million tokens")
is very hard to visualize.
So let's compare LLMs to web search. I'm choosing search as the
comparison since it's in the same vicinity and since it's
something everyone uses and nobody pays for, not because I'm suggesting that
ungrounded generative AI is a good substitute for search.
(It should also go without saying that these are just my personal
opinions.)
What is the price of a web search?
Here's the public API pricing for some companies operating their own
web search infrastructure, retrieved on 2025-05-02:
The
Gemini API pricing
lists a "Grounding with Google Search" feature at $35/1k queries. I
believe that's the best number we can get for Google, they don't publish
prices for a "raw" search result API.
The
Bing Search API
is priced at $15/1k queries at the cheapest tier.
Brave
has a price of $5/1k searches at the cheapest tier. Though there's something very
strange about their pricing structure, with the unit pricing increasing as
the quota increases, which is the opposite of what you'd expect. The
tier with real quota is priced at $9/1k searches.
So there's a range of prices, but not a horribly wide one, and with the
engines you'd expect to be of higher quality also having higher prices.
What is the price of LLMs in a similar domain?
To make a reasonable comparison between those search prices and LLM
prices, we need two numbers:
How many tokens are output per query?
What's the price per token?
I picked a few arbitrary queries from my search history, and phrased
them as questions, and ran them on Gemini 2.5 Flash (thinking mode off)
in AI Studio:
[When was the term LLM first used?] -> 361 tokens, 2.5
seconds
[What are the top javascript game engines?] -> 1145 tokens, 7.6
seconds
[What are the typical carry-on bag size limits in europe?] -> 506
tokens, 3.4 seconds
[List the 10 largest power outages in history] -> 583 tokens, 3.7
seconds
Note that I'm not judging the quality of the answers here. The
purpose is just to get rough numbers for how large typical responses
are. A 500-1000 token range seems like a reasonable estimate.
What's the price of a token? The pricing is sometimes different for input
and output tokens. Input tokens tend to be cheaper, and our inputs are
very short compared to the outputs, so for simplicity let's consider all
the tokens to be outputs. Here's the pricing of some relevant models,
retrieved on 2025-05-02:

If we assume the average query uses 1k tokens, these prices would be
directly comparable to the prices per 1k search queries. That's convenient.
The low end of that spectrum is at least an order of magnitude
cheaper than even the cheapest search API, and even the models at the
low end are pretty capable. The high end is about on par with the
highest end of search pricing. To compare a midrange pair on quality,
the Bing Search vs. a Gemini 2.5 Flash comparison shows the LLM being
1/25th the price.
Note that many of the above models have cheaper pricing in exchange
for more flexible scheduling (Anthropic, Google and OpenAI give a 50%
discount for batch requests, Deepseek is 50%-75% cheaper during off-peak
hours). I've not included those cheaper options in the table to keep
things comparable, but the presence of those cheaper tiers is worth
keeping in mind when thinking about the next section...

data.author: dmarcos
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种先进的3D Gaussian Splatting渲染器，可集成到THREE.js场景中，与其它网格和溅点共存。该渲染器支持在所有设备上快速渲染，具备可编程的动态溅点效果，并支持多种格式（如ply、spz、splat、ksplat）。用户可以轻松上手，实现高效的3D视觉效果。

data.title: V-JEPA 2 world model and new benchmarks for physical reasoning
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：V-JEPA 2模型在机器人任务中的表现及其未来潜力

不同观点：
• TheAceOfHearts：对V-JEPA 2在全新环境中65%-80%的成功率表示关注，认为20%的失败率较高。同时提到计算和执行时间从4分钟减少到16秒是一个显著的进步。对未来能否实现>99%的成功率表示兴趣，并指出目前依赖图像目标的局限性，但认可作者已认识到这一问题。
• siavosh：关注"语义"嵌入是如何学习的，认为这是主要的技术挑战。
• fidotron：猜测模型是否会重新创造Verlet积分或生成光学加速度抵消类型的启发式方法，并提出将对象跟踪与物理理解结合可以测量物理量的想法。
• iLoveOncall：质疑"世界模型"和"物理推理"的概念，认为模型并不真正理解物理，只是根据训练数据进行复述，类似于图像或视频生成模型。
• cubefox：支持JEPA的基本理念，即预测嵌入而非具体标记，认为这是动物行为的方式。指出视频帧预测的计算复杂性，并强调机器人技术中对未来感官数据的预测需求。
• jcelerier：提到物理直觉的发展需要时间，即使在儿童中也是如此，但比训练大型语言模型的时间要长。
• artificialprint：建议使用ARC-AGI 2进行测试。
• ldjkfkdsjnv：批评Meta的领导层在非LLM AI模型研究上浪费资源。
• momojo：质疑Meta投资这项研究的动机和潜在回报。

补充讨论：
• 对V-JEPA 2的成功率和计算效率的评价存在争议，有人认为20%的失败率较高，但也有观点认为从15%到80%的提升是显著进步。
• 对模型如何学习物理概念和技术实现细节（如"语义"嵌入和物理启发式方法）存在技术性讨论。
• 对"物理理解"和"世界模型"的真实含义及其实现方式存在哲学性争议，有人认为当前模型并不真正理解物理，只是复述数据。
• 对Meta投资这项研究的战略价值和潜在应用存在质疑和批评。

• siavosh：关注"语义"嵌入是如何学习的，认为这是主要的技术挑战。
• fidotron：猜测模型是否会重新创造Verlet积分或生成光学加速度抵消类型的启发式方法，并提出将对象跟踪与物理理解结合可以测量物理量的想法。
• iLoveOncall：质疑"世界模型"和"物理推理"的概念，认为模型并不真正理解物理，只是根据训练数据进行复述，类似于图像或视频生成模型。
• cubefox：支持JEPA的基本理念，即预测嵌入而非具体标记，认为这是动物行为的方式。指出视频帧预测的计算复杂性，并强调机器人技术中对未来感官数据的预测需求。
• jcelerier：提到物理直觉的发展需要时间，即使在儿童中也是如此，但比训练大型语言模型的时间要长。
• artificialprint：建议使用ARC-AGI 2进行测试。
• ldjkfkdsjnv：批评Meta的领导层在非LLM AI模型研究上浪费资源。
• momojo：质疑Meta投资这项研究的动机和潜在回报。

补充讨论：
• 对V-JEPA 2的成功率和计算效率的评价存在争议，有人认为20%的失败率较高，但也有观点认为从15%到80%的提升是显著进步。
• 对模型如何学习物理概念和技术实现细节（如"语义"嵌入和物理启发式方法）存在技术性讨论。
• 对"物理理解"和"世界模型"的真实含义及其实现方式存在哲学性争议，有人认为当前模型并不真正理解物理，只是复述数据。
• 对Meta投资这项研究的战略价值和潜在应用存在质疑和批评。

data.author: FinnKuhn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dollywood主题公园及其火车设施，美国乘客铁路的现状与未来，以及与欧洲等地区的比较。

不同观点：
• [chrisco255] 认为美国由于城市结构、汽车拥有率和高 sprawl（低密度扩展）等原因，乘客铁路难以发展。他指出，公交车在美国更实用，未来可能更多依赖自动小型巴士和电动车，而非铁路。尽管他个人希望看到一些城市通过高速铁路连接，但认为缺乏实现的意愿和动力。

• [flippyhead] 对将Dollywood Express的乘客量与27个州相比的表达方式感到有趣，并建议将这种比较方式应用于其他事物，以提供更直观的理解。

• [throwaway522482] 分享了住在Sevier County的个人体验，提到Dolly Parton对当地居民的慈善活动，如提供折扣票。同时提到Dollywood Express的受欢迎程度，并指出乘坐蒸汽火车时会被煤烟覆盖。

• [deelowe] 描述了参观Dollywood的积极体验，强调了公园的清洁度、员工的友好性和设施的良好维护，特别是蒸汽火车的独特体验。

• [jonah-archive] 分享了自己乘坐Dollywood Express的经历，提供了关于火车技术细节的链接，并提到乘坐时的安全说明和趣味体验。

• [jancsika] 用幽默的方式指出，在现实生活中，货运列车在美国拥有优先权，Dollywood Express的趣味性在于它不受此限制。

• [sarchertech] 建议在比较Dollywood Express时，也应考虑Tennessee Valley Railroad，并提供了相关链接，指出其提供的风景路线和理论上的通勤可能性。

• [toomuchtodo] 简短地表示推荐Dollywood，认为是一个很好的游玩选择。

• [lisper] 认为将Dollywood Express的乘客量与州际铁路相比是不公平的，因为前者是游乐设施，而非交通工具，其经济模式与实际交通系统不同。

• [cjj_swe] 表达了对Dolly Parton和家乡的热爱。

• [xnx] 关注Dollywood Express的煤炭消耗量，指出其对环境的影响，并提供了计算细节。

• [johng] 认为Dolly Parton非常受欢迎，如果她竞选总统可能会获胜，基于其广泛的公众好感度。

• [NoblePublius] 对比了美国和欧洲的铁路基础设施，指出美国更多选择个人交通工具是由于其经济能力和自由选择权，而非政府不投资公共交通。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于美国乘客铁路的发展前景和可行性，以及与欧洲等地区的比较。部分评论者认为美国社会结构和选择导致铁路不发达，而另一些人则对铁路交通的潜力抱有期望。
- 对Dollywood Express的讨论集中在乘坐体验、技术细节和环境影响等方面。
- 个人体验和观点分享丰富了讨论，提供了多角度的见解。

data.title: The Beach Boys' Brian Wilson Dies at 82
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 布莱恩·威尔逊（Brian Wilson），海滩男孩（The Beach Boys）的联合创始人及主要词曲作者，于2024年去世，享年82岁。他生前患有类似痴呆的神经认知障碍。威尔逊在青少年时期与兄弟和朋友组建了乐队，凭借《Surfin' U.S.A.》等歌曲成名。1964年，他因恐慌症退出巡演，专注于制作，推出了实验性专辑《Pet Sounds》，虽初期反响不佳，但后来被视为经典。原计划的续作《Smile》因故未完成，直到2004年才重见天日。威尔逊一生饱受心理健康问题困扰，曾受控于心理学家尤金·兰迪，后通过法律手段摆脱其控制。海滩男孩共发行29张录音室专辑，威尔逊个人也发布了多张专辑，并获得多项荣誉，包括格莱美奖和摇滚名人堂入选。他的逝世令乐坛和全球乐迷深感惋惜。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对布莱恩·威尔逊（Brian Wilson）及其音乐作品的评价和纪念

不同观点：
• **布莱恩·威尔逊是流行音乐的伟大作曲家**：[gabriel666smith]认为威尔逊是史上最伟大的流行音乐作曲家，甚至将他与巴赫和Bacharach相提并论。他强调威尔逊的音乐在技术上的精湛以及情感上的深度，尤其是在他晚年作品中仍然保持极高的艺术水准。

• **《Pet Sounds》专辑的重新评价**：[alexjplant]提到自己曾经对《Pet Sounds》不以为然，认为人们只是为了显得有品位而假装喜欢，直到成熟后才真正理解并爱上这张专辑。他将这张专辑形容为“proto-emo”并 dressed up in an instrumental psychoedelic doo-wop trenchcoat。

• **布莱恩·威尔逊是海滩男孩的核心**：[jihadjihad]引用丹尼斯·威尔逊的话，认为布莱恩是海滩男孩的灵魂，其他成员只是他的“信使”。这一观点强调了布莱恩在乐队中的核心地位。

• **推荐威尔逊的后期作品**：[andy_xor_andrew]鼓励听众去听威尔逊1988年的同名专辑以及2004年重制的《Smile!》，认为这些作品在音乐性和作曲上都非常出色，值得一听。

• **布莱恩·威尔逊的音乐影响深远**：[JKCalhoun]、[Lammy]、[automathematics]等人分享了威尔逊的音乐对他们个人成长的影响，并对他晚年的复出和广泛认可表示欣慰。

补充讨论：
• **对威尔逊生平的感慨**：[Lammy]提到威尔逊与Eugene Landy的悲剧故事，但庆幸他晚年重获爱戴。其他评论如[telesilla]则直接表达对威尔逊经典作品如《God Only Knows》的喜爱。

• **与其他音乐人的比较**：[nonameiguess]将威尔逊与Trent Reznor进行比较，认为虽然两者都有着独特的艺术风格和隐退倾向，但当今乐坛很难找到类似影响力的年轻音乐人。

• **对具体作品的深入解读**：[scop]对《Wouldn't it be Nice》的歌词进行分析，认为其表面欢快的旋律下隐藏着对理想生活的渴望和失落，展示了威尔逊音乐的深度和复杂性。

争议焦点：
• **《Pet Sounds》的初期评价**：部分听众如[alexjplant]起初对《Pet Sounds》持怀疑态度，认为其受欢迎部分是因为文化资本，直到自己成熟后才真正理解。

• **威尔逊与其他音乐天才的比较**：[nonameiguess]提出当今乐坛缺乏类似威尔逊或Reznor这样有影响力的年轻音乐人，这一观点可能引发对现代音乐和艺术家的广泛讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕布莱恩·威尔逊的音乐才华、作品深度及其对个人和乐坛的影响展开，既有对其伟大成就的高度赞扬，也有对其作品的个人化解读和反思。

Save this story

Save this story

Brian Wilson
, the co-founder and primary songwriter of
the Beach Boys
, has died, his family
announced
. While an official cause of death was not disclosed, the beloved musical auteur, who helped pioneer the studio-as-instrument, influencing generations of musicians in pop and beyond, was
revealed
in early 2024 to be living with a neurocognitive disorder akin to dementia. Wilson was 82 years old.
“We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away,” his family wrote in a statement shared on Wilson’s official
Facebook
. “We are at a loss for words right now. Please respect our privacy at this time as our family is grieving. We realize that we are sharing our grief with the world. Love & Mercy.”
Born in Inglewood, California, Wilson formed the band—then called the Pendletones—as a teenager with his brothers Dennis and Carl, their cousin Mike Love, and high school friend Al Jardine. Their first song, “Surfin’,” was released by Candix Records, who changed the band’s name to the Beach Boys without the members’ permission. A year later, the band signed with Capitol to release its debut,
Surfin’ Safari
; the following year, “Surfin’ U.S.A.” became the Beach Boys’ first U.S. Top 10 single. In 1963, the band released three albums:
Surfin’ U.S.A.
,
Surfer Girl
, and
Little Deuce Coupe.
By then, Wilson had started his career as a producer for other musicians. He worked with Jan and Dean, the Castellas, Donna Loren, Sharon Marie, and others.
In 1964, Brian Wilson decided to stop touring with the Beach Boys after experiencing a panic attack due to the band’s heavy schedule. He focused on his production, and in 1965� started work on the landmark experimental pop album
Pet Sounds
. Wilson was the mastermind behind the
Pet Sounds
sessions, working alongside famed studio musicians the Wrecking Crew. At the time of its release,
Pet Sounds
was considered a relative commercial flop and critical failure. In 2004, it was inducted into the Library of Congress’ National Recording Registry due to its cultural, historical, and aesthetic significance.
“I wanted to grow musically, so I experimented,” Wilson told the
Harvard Business Review
in 2016. “I wasn’t the type to sit around and be satisfied with an accomplishment, especially not in the studio. And I had ideas coming into my head all the time. Many had to do with using instruments as voices and voices as instruments. I would put sounds together to create something new. Some ideas didn’t work, because they were too difficult to achieve at the time. But most did. And then I immediately moved to the next thing.”
Wilson planned a follow-up album called
Smile
,
which he described as a “teenage symphony to God,” but it was scrapped after continual delays. After the album’s cancellation in 1967, Wilson’s role in the band receded. In 1968, he entered a psychiatric hospital for treatment. In the years after the release of
Pet Sounds
, Wilson briefly owned and operated a health food store called the Radiant Radish. He continued to work with the band while struggling with drug and alcohol addiction in the ’70s.
After a family intervention into Wilson’s deteriorating mental and physical health, he became embroiled with the controversial psychologist Eugene Landy. Their decades-long treatment later became the subject of a biographical film called
Love & Mercy
. The Beach Boys enjoyed a brief resurgence after their 1977 album
Love You
, but Wilson’s health issues persisted. In 1982, Landy removed him from the band for intensive treatment and exercised increasing control over Wilson’s financial and creative endeavors, prompting Wilson to release his debut solo album in 1988. In 1992, following legal action from Carl Wilson and other members of the Wilson family, Landy’s psychology license was revoked and he received a restraining order from Wilson.
Wilson eventually revisited
Smile,
reworking the archived studio sessions with Darian Sahanaja to bring the once-scrapped project to a live concert. He released
Brian Wilson: Presents Smile
in 2004 to critical acclaim. He continued to release solo work in the 2000s. His last solo album of original material was 2015’s
No Pier Pressure
, which featured contributions from Kacey Musgraves and Zooey Deschanel, while his final solo album of covers was 2021’s
At My Piano
, in which he played a variety of the Beach Boys’ songs on the instrument. He released a
memoir
in 2016, and the following year shared “
Some Sweet Day
,” a previously unreleased song recorded in the 1990s, as well as a new single called “
Run James Run
.”
The Beach Boys went on to record 29 studio albums, 11 live albums, and 75 singles. Wilson and the band were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 1988. As a solo artist, Wilson
won
two Grammy awards (out of nine nominations), and the Beach Boys were honored in 2001 with a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2000, Wilson was inducted into the Songwriters

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Samuel Pepys 及其日记的多方面讨论，包括其个人行为、历史价值、发音、特定日记条目及相关资源。

不同观点：
• [sherr] 认为 Pepys 虽有许多令人钦佩的品质，但其对女性的恶劣行为不应被忽视。今天他可能会被称为“性掠食者”甚至“强奸犯”。这种行为在18世纪被视为常见，因为女性常被视为性对象。sherr 通过 Guy de la Bédoyère 的 YouTube 视频了解到这一点，并认为有必要揭示真相。
• [vehemenz] 分享了另一个关于 Pepys 的学术视频，其中包含一些精美的古籍版本的日记。

• [sherr] 的评论引发了对 Pepys 个人行为与其历史贡献之间如何平衡评价的讨论。对 Pepys 对待女性行为的揭露和定性成为争议的焦点，部分观众可能对其英雄形象产生了质疑。

Feature
The Hidden Diary of Samuel Pepys
When Samuel Pepys’ diary was first published 200 years ago it was an instant hit, but rumours soon spread about what had been cut and why.
Kate Loveman
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 6 June 2025
I
n June 1825 Samuel Pepys’ diary was published for the first time. It was an instant hit. Newspapers were soon full of reviews quoting memorable passages from this secret journal: Pepys’ descriptions of the Great Fire of London, his new wig, and his first ever ‘Cupp of Tee’ were among the favourites. Further editions followed, and by the end of the 19th century the diary was celebrated as a classic of British history and literature. Today, Pepys is the star of museum exhibits and historical novels. Excerpts from his diary are often used to introduce students to the Restoration period and, indeed, to introduce history: across England, six-year-olds following the National Curriculum can tell you about how Pepys buried his expensive cheese to protect it from the fire.

data.title: Medical Aid in Dying, My Health, and So On
data.author: homebrewer
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己选择“医疗援助死亡”（Medical Aid in Dying）的决策过程及其健康状况的恶化。作者在2021年11月因严重心脏问题入院，被诊断为心力衰竭并接受了心脏搭桥手术。术后恢复不佳，安装了植入式心律转复除颤器（ICD）。然而，ICD多次电击让他饱受痛苦，且心脏问题反复发作。2024年初，他的病情进一步恶化，经历了一次特别痛苦的夜晚，被多次电击。医生建议再次进行心脏消融手术，并预估他可能还有十年寿命。面对不断恶化的健康状况和生活质量，作者决定选择“尊严死亡”，并将于2025年6月13日结束自己的生命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：医疗干预、死亡自主权、以及相关医疗设备和法律的讨论。

不同观点：
• [daedrdev] 认为心脏移植手术需要对过程作出全面承诺，而他们不愿意做出这种承诺。他们提到可能是因为对进一步医疗干预的创伤感到恐惧，因此选择不接受移植手术，即使这意味着可能会面临死亡。

• [strongpigeon] 支持医疗援助下的死亡选择，认为这种选择赋予了人们不仅在如何生活上，也在如何死亡上拥有自主权。他们分享了亲近之人选择这种死亡方式的经历，强调了这种方式让告别变得更有计划和意义。

• [jollyllama] 对植入式除颤器的频繁电击表示困惑，质疑这种频繁的电击是否会对患者产生负面影响，显示出对医疗设备实际效果的关注。

• [hypeatei] 对俄勒冈州的“尊严死亡”计划表示赞赏，并询问其他州是否有类似法律，同时表达了对安乐死合法化的广泛支持，认为这种法律是向正确方向迈进的一步。

• [scottcha] 对近年来某些症状（如心动过速）的发生率表示疑问，询问是否有相关数据支持，并质疑这些症状的发生率是否自2021年以来有所增加。

• [gadders] 建议对植入式除颤器增加一个15或30秒的音频警告，以便使用者能有所准备，显示出对医疗设备人性化设计的关注。

• [fnord77] 表达了对当前医学无法有效治疗许多疾病的恐惧，反映出对医学现状的担忧和无奈。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是是否选择医疗干预，如心脏移植和植入式除颤器，以及这些干预对患者生活质量的影响。
- 另一个讨论点是安乐死和“尊严死亡”计划的合法性和道德性，以及这种选择对患者及其家属的心理和情感影响。
- 对医疗设备（如除颤器）的改进建议和对症状发生率的统计数据的需求也成为讨论的重要部分。
- 整体讨论反映出对医疗自主权、患者生活质量和医学局限性的深刻关注。

44249303.article_content:
Medical Aid in Dying, My Health, and so on
I’ll start at the end, because that’s the most important part.  Later this month, I’m obtaining medical aid in dying AKA death with dignity.  Barring unforeseen circumstances or unexpected changes, my last day on earth will be June 13th, 2025.  Realize that I’m just over 46 years old.  So how the hell did we get here?  I’ve written part of the story in dribs and drabs over the years, so I may as well write up the whole thing.
Late on the night of November 14th, 2021, I went to the local emergency room.  I had a blood pressure of 55/37 and a pulse of 220.  I had a heart attack at some point.  I’m not quite sure when that happened.  They admitted me for a hospital stay.
One of the first things they did was an arteriogram, and they found blockage in one artery.  They thought they would be able to treat it with stent placement during the procedure, but it was too severe for that.  They had a surgeon consult with me about doing an open heart procedure.  It would be a single bypass.  If I refused the procedure, my life expectancy would be about 4 and a half years.  So it seemed reasonable to go ahead with it.
On Thursday, I went in for surgery.  It was miserable, but I survived it.  By Monday afternoon, I had recovered sufficiently to be released from the hospital, so I went home and finished the recovery process there.
During my hospital stay, I was also diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.  My ejection fraction was between 25 and 30 percent.  They told me that they would probably want to place an ICD (implantable cardioverter defibrillator) if my ejection fraction didn’t improve.  It never really did.  The best it got was 30 to 35 percent.  So in February of 2023 I went in for an out patient stay to have a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (SICD) placed.
Fastforward a few months.  I’m sitting in my recliner, eating some plantain chips, when all of a sudden, I got shocked.  I jumped and screamed.  Still, it only happened once, and I’m thinking: this is no big deal.  A few weeks later, in August, I received another shock.  It only happened once, so again, I’m like “no big deal.”
On September 11th, the situation changed.  I felt “off” all evening.  I was shocked once, and I kept feeling like another one was coming.  So I went to the ER.  My ICD device fired while I was on the ambulance and when I was being wheeled into the ER.  They kept me for a couple days, ran some tests, told me to follow up with cardiology, and sent me home.
A week later, I was back in the ER with the same complaint.  I don’t remember whether there were multiple shocks.  The same thing happened: they kept me for a couple days to make sure I was stable, ran some tests, sent me home, and told me to follow up with cardiology.
On the first Friday of October, I kept feeling “off”, as though I was going to have a heart episode.  The device didn’t fire, but I went to the ER anyway.  When I was in the ambulance, they told me that I was in VTac (ventricular tachycardia), and they shocked me.  I was shocked several times by hospital staff while they tried to get me stable.  This time was a little different.  The cardiac electrophysiologist decided that it was time to do a cardiac ablation.  They performed that procedure on the following Monday or Tuesday, and I went home in the middle of the week.
Things seemed ok for the next couple of months.  Then, on the night of February 1, 2024, I started receiving more shocks from the ICD.  I went back to the ER.  That night, my ICD shocked me at least seventeen times, and I was also shocked several additional times by paramedics and ER staff.  If you’ve ever taken a physical beating that has left you sore for days, you know exactly what I went through that night.  I took a beating or two of that sort when I was younger, and that’s exactly how being shocked more than twenty times felt.  Every movement of my upper body hurt for the next several days, including just shifting around in bed.  The day after I landed in the emergency room, they sent me to a much larger university hospital in Portland.  That hospital stabilized me, switched out my ICD for another device, and sent me home a couple days later.
I spent the next few months in a state of total mental paralysis that I suspect was some kind of PTSD.  I kept feeling like I was going to have heart episodes and waiting for the next shock.  The new device they placed when I was in Portland had some pacing functionality, so I’m pretty sure I avoided some shocks.  When I saw my cardiologist in the summer of 2024, she told me that the pacing functionality barely succeeded keeping me out of a round of shocks.  She and her boss wanted to do another cardiac ablation.
At this point, I started wondering just how much life I had left.  I bluntly asked for an estimation of my life expectancy and was told maybe ten years with the ablation and the defibrillator.  The point of the ablation wa

data.title: Publish a Python Wheel to GCP Artifact Registry with Poetry
data.author: sergiolema
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Poetry构建Python项目的可运行文件（wheel文件），并将其集成到CI/CD流水线中，最终在GCP虚拟机上运行。由于项目需要直接与GPU驱动交互，不能使用Docker，因此作者选择创建wheel文件。具体步骤包括：

1. 使用Poetry配置`pyproject.toml`文件，指定要打包的目录。
2. 在GCP的Artifact Registry中创建Python仓库，用于存储wheel文件。
3. 配置Poetry的`poetry.toml`文件，指定自定义仓库地址。
4. 动态更新`pyproject.toml`中的版本号，以避免覆盖已发布的版本。
5. 配置VM实例的权限和`pip`设置，以从Artifact Registry下载wheel文件。
6. 使用`pip install`安装项目并运行。

最终，通过这种方式实现了类似Docker工作流的构建、发布和运行流程，满足了直接与GPU驱动交互的需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：发布Python包的注册表选择以及是否需要将所有项目容器化

不同观点：
• joshdavham 提出问题，询问是否有人将Python包发布到PyPI以外的其他注册表。他表示自己只使用过PyPI，对其他注册表的使用情况感到好奇。

• seanp2k2 认为现在将所有东西都容器化（如使用Docker）已成为默认做法，但这种趋势令人遗憾。他建议创建一个类似于 "You Might Not Need jQuery" 的网站，提醒人们不一定需要Docker。

• sergiolema 分享了自己的项目需求，指出由于需要直接与机器和GPU驱动交互，无法使用Docker。他选择了创建可执行的Python文件，并使用Poetry生成wheel文件，同时将其集成到CI/CD管道中。

• westurner 提到GCP Artifact Registry作为一个OCI容器镜像注册表，支持将容器镜像推送到该注册表的GitHub Actions。他还讨论了使用 "pypa/cibuildwheel" 在CI中构建跨平台Python包的简便性，并询问GCP Artifact Registry是否支持 artifact attestations（ artifact证明）。

补充讨论：

• 讨论还涉及到不同的工具和平台选择，如joshdavham对PyPI以外注册表的好奇，以及westurner对GCP Artifact Registry功能和GitHub Actions的介绍，显示出开发者在发布和构建Python包时有多种选择和考量。

• 另一个技术细节是artifact attestations（ artifact证明）的使用和重要性，westurner对此提出疑问，显示出在CI/CD管道中建立构建来源的可信度也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

44222074.article_content:
Recently, I’ve been building a project in Python that doesn’t have a Docker image as output. Instead, I need a runnable file. Why? Because I need to talk to the machine directly and not to Docker. Because I need to talk to the GPU drivers directly and not to another abstraction layer.
So, I needed to create a runnable file in Python. I needed to create a wheel file. All this with
Poetry
and integrate it into my CI/CD pipeline.
Let’s break down the steps.
Building the Project With Poetry
My first solution was, when an VM is created in my
Compute Instance Group
, I clone the git project, install Poetry, sync the project and run it. Just like in my laptop.
But! I need a token to clone the project. I never liked this solution. So, I’ve been thinking around for an alternative.
I wanted a solution near to the Docker workflow: build locally, push to a registry, and download the latest version at the startup. I searched a way to do the same with a python project. here come the wheel files.
By default, I build my project with
poetry sync
, because I don’t need a runnable file as I mainly use Docker images. But Poetry allows me to configure the
install
command a little bit further. Let’s start configuring that command to build a wheel file.
Here is an extract of the
pyproject.toml
file:
[tool.poetry]
# ...
packages = [
{ include = "main_dir" },
]
It indicates to Poetry to include the main_dir directory when building a package, when building a wheel. Now the
poetry build
command does not require the
no-root
parameter anymore. And the wheel file will be available in the
dist
folder.
Create a Python Registry to Store My Wheel File
The project is hosted in GCP. And GCP has an
artifact registry
that allows me to specify which type of files I want to save there: Docker images, Python Wheel files, Java JAR files…
Once the artifact registry is created, I need to configure two things: Poetry to push to the adequate place, and the VM to pull from the correct place.
Let’s start in the Poetry side. Poetry has another configuration file,
poetry.toml
, which is optional and accepts this kind of configuration:
[repositories.my-registry]
url = "https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-project/my-registry/"
Now, after building my Poetry project, I can publish to the registry. How?
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
But! (Yes, another but) I need to remove the
dist
folder, which is the default output folder to build the wheel file. Otherwise, it will ask if I want to override the existing files. and until now, there is no option to force a “yes, override the files, go ahead”.
rm -fr dist/
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
But! (let’s continue with the buts) Each version I publish will have the version number set in the
pyproject.toml
file. Overriding versioned files is never a good practice. So, I must use a dynamic version number in my
pyproject.toml
file.
sed -I.back 's/^version = "[^"]*"/version = "1.0.post'"$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)"'"/' pyproject.toml
rm -fr dist/
poetry publish --build --repository my-registry
That’s all on the side of publication. What about pulling the file?
As I’m in a VM running in GCP, and the artifact registry is also in GCP, I must add the adequate permissions to do the operation.
Once, configured all the IAM stuff, I need to run the following command in the VM (it will help me for the next steps).
gcloud artifacts print-settings python --project=my-gcp-project \
--repository=my-registry \
--location=europe-west1
This will print all the configuration I need to put into my VM instance. It will look something like this:
cat > $HOME/.pypirc<< EOF
[distutils]
index-servers =
my-registry
[my-registry]
repository: https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-gcp-project/my-registry/
EOF
mkdir $HOME/.pip
cat > $HOME/.pip/pip.conf<< EOF
[global]
extra-index-url = https://europe-west1-python.pkg.dev/my-gcp-registry/my-registry/simple/
EOF
Ok, now both my CI/CD and my VM instance are ready to send a Python wheel file from one to the other.
Download a Python Wheel file and Run It
Once the file is available in the GCP Artifact Registry, I need to pull it and run it. It’s quite simple now.
pip install my-project
This first command will install in the machine (no need of Poetry in the production instance) my project.
pip
will look for the latest version of
my-project
into both the pip repository and into the extra index
my-registry
.
In my case, I’ve added my-registry as an extra index. Why? Because my project needs a lot of dependencies (Flask, SQLAlchemy, Pandas…), and I don’t want to store all of them into my GCP Artifact Registry (and pay for that). So, I let
pip
download what’s available in the public registry, and add an extra registry where to look for the other libraries (which is my project).
Once the project is downloaded, I can run it simply as a Python project.
python -m my_job
I have this command because my root module is called
my_job
and I have a
__main__
file which is the starting point of
44222074.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Poetry构建Python项目的可运行文件（wheel文件），并将其集成到CI/CD流水线中，最终在GCP虚拟机上运行。由于项目需要直接与GPU驱动交互，不能使用Docker，因此作者选择创建wheel文件。具体步骤包括：

1. 使用Poetry配置`pyproject.toml`文件，指定要打包的目录。
2. 在GCP的Artifact Registry中创建Python仓库，用于存储wheel文件。
3. 配置Poetry的`poetry.toml`文件，指定自定义仓库地址。
4. 动态更新`pyproject.toml`中的版本号，以避免覆盖已发布的版本。
5. 配置VM实例的权限和`pip`设置，以从Artifact Registry下载wheel文件。
6. 使用`pip install`安装项目并运行。

最终，通过这种方式实现了类似Docker工作流的构建、发布和运行流程，满足了直接与GPU驱动交互的需求。

• seanp2k2 认为现在将所有东西都容器化（如使用Docker）已成为默认做法，但这种趋势令人遗憾。他建议创建一个类似于 "You Might Not Need jQuery" 的网站，提醒人们不一定需要Docker。

• sergiolema 分享了自己的项目需求，指出由于需要直接与机器和GPU驱动交互，无法使用Docker。他选择了创建可执行的Python文件，并使用Poetry生成wheel文件，同时将其集成到CI/CD管道中。

• westurner 提到GCP Artifact Registry作为一个OCI容器镜像注册表，支持将容器镜像推送到该注册表的GitHub Actions。他还讨论了使用 "pypa/cibuildwheel" 在CI中构建跨平台Python包的简便性，并询问GCP Artifact Registry是否支持 artifact attestations（ artifact证明）。

data.title: DeskHog, an open-source developer toy
data.author: constantinum
data.article_summary: DeskHog是一款开源、3D打印、手掌大小的开发者玩具，内置ESP32-S3处理器、240x135彩色TFT显示屏、WiFi和LED，拥有10小时电池续航。它可以运行简单游戏如Pong和Flappy Bird，并支持I²C扩展端口。DeskHog不仅是微型游戏机，还能作为桌面终端查看PostHog数据，具备实用商业工具如尴尬避免器和Pomodoro计时器。DIY版本现已推出，完整套件即将发布。未来可能推出DeskHog Pro及配件，如更多按钮和表带。用户可在其开源平台上自行开发游戏和工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather设备的能力和用途的讨论，以及对Posthog公司及其硬件产品的各种看法。

不同观点：
• [技术可行性讨论] mananaysiempre提出该设备是否能运行Doom游戏，并讨论了其硬件配置（如双核Xtensa处理器、内存和存储）是否足以支持该游戏。他认为存储可能是一个限制因素，但或许可以缩减游戏以适应设备。

• [用途和定位质疑] joshdavham对该设备的存在意义提出质疑，尤其是Posthog作为一家主要从事网络分析软件的公司，为何要开发硬件产品。

• [公司名称反应] rideontime对Posthog公司的名称表示惊讶和调侃。

• [公司工作环境评价] bradleykingz认为在Posthog工作可能很有趣。

• [支持和赞赏] sibelius对Posthog的D轮融资成功表示祝贺，并对公司给予高度评价。

• [技术问题提醒] fnord77提到其Pihole系统屏蔽了与该设备相关的域名，暗示可能存在网络安全或隐私问题。

• [设备评价和类比] bitwize将该设备比作“Hog Speed”游戏中的角色，认为其概念一般且可能用途有限，同时将其类比为mini Chumby，暗示其可能具有不确定的广泛应用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：主要是针对ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather设备的实际用途和技术可行性。有人对其运行复杂程序（如Doom）的能力表示兴趣，同时也有人对其市场定位和用途表示质疑。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：包括对Posthog公司名称的调侃、对其融资成功的祝贺，以及对设备域名被屏蔽的技术提醒。这些反映出社区对该设备及相关公司的多角度关注。

DeskHog
It's a developer
toy

joy
Full kits coming soon. DIY version available now.

DeskHog is an
open-source,
3D printed,
palm-sized
slice of developer joy
Open-source
We're open-source, and so is DeskHog. It's yours to hack. Build your own games and tools with AI editors (or C++ if you're a masochist).
3D printed
Danilo prints these at home and assembles them by hand. It's a friction-fit labor of love. Or you can print your own from the files on GitHub.
Palm-sized
DeskHog is small enough to fit in your pocket. It's got a 10-hour battery life, WiFi, and a cute flashing LED so you can find it in the dark.
But what is DeskHog really?
It's a teeny, tiny, beast.
DeskHog packs a ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather in a custom-made 3D printed case. It comes complete with a 240x135 color TFT display, a 10-hour battery life, WiFi, and a cute little LED.
It's a hand-made micro games console. It's a desktop terminal for PostHog data. It's a friend.
Can it play Pong?
Yes.
Can it play Flappy Bird?
Yes.
Can it play Doom?
...We're working on it.
Want
more
hardware?
We included an I²C expansion port, just for people like you.
Of course, we're making some games for it too
We're still nailing down the launch lineup, but you can
build your own
while you wait

Does pineapple belong on pizza? Sophie thinks so.

Build your own

(A great excuse to expense your DeskHog purchase)

Hate smalltalk? These icebreakers will help.
Built by:
Annika Schmid
Pomodoro Timer
Gives you time to ponder 20 tomatoes.
Built by:
Annika Schmid

Grab graphs from PostHog and squint at them.
Built by:

Your phone and data are
DeskHog's best friends
DeskHog can get online via a captive portal and pull insights from your PostHog projects. Scan the QR code with your phone to connect and link data to the Insight Keeper-upper.
The DIY version of DeskHog already supports simple insights, like big numbers and trends (squinting required), but we're working on more. And we're open source, so you can help!

DeskHog Pro will connect via the I²C port, adding more buttons, and a huge dial so you can crank up the vibes. We're also thinking about making a watch strap, so you can wear DeskHog on your wrist.

• [adjagu] 提到甘地、乔布斯、特蕾莎修女、亚里士多德和梅·韦斯特等历史人物，并暗示他们曾使用并享受过Markdown。此评论带有幽默和夸张性质，意在引起对Markdown使用者范围广泛的关注。
• [sirkiller] 提到在访问Markdown相关网站时遇到了SSL证书错误，具体为“SEC_ERROR_UNKNOWN_CRITICAL_EXTENSION”错误代码。
• [johng] 进一步解释了[sirkiller]的问题，指出是因为该网站没有SSL配置，从而导致出现错误提示。
• [some_furry] 提出关于Markdown工具之间的比较问题，询问Markdown.ninja与Buttondown之间的区别和优劣。

补充讨论：
• 评论中出现了对Markdown工具的技术性问题讨论，特别是与网站SSL安全证书相关的错误。
• 另外，有人对不同Markdown服务或工具的比较表示关注，表明用户在选择工具时可能会考虑功能和使用体验的差异。
• 整个讨论中存在一定的幽默成分，如[adjagu]对历史名人使用Markdown的调侃，使得讨论氛围轻松。

data.author: ryan_j_naughton
data.article_summary: 考古学家马克·霍顿（Mark Horton）及其团队经过十年研究，认为失踪的罗阿诺克殖民者可能融入了克罗托安印第安社会，而非遭遇悲剧。他们在北卡罗来纳州的哈特拉斯岛（原称克罗托安岛）发现了铁屑（hammerscale），这是锻造铁器时产生的微小碎片，证明殖民者曾在该地进行金属加工，而这是当时当地印第安人无法掌握的技术。此外，出土的16世纪英国文物如枪支、酒壶、珠子等也支持这一结论。霍顿认为，殖民者并未灭亡，而是成功融入了当地社会。
